newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 1.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Friday:
* U.S. stocks generally rose on Thursday, despite a 32.28-point drop in the Dow Industrials, on data showing that growth had slowed in the second quarter and inflation was tame.
* The signs of little inflation also helped the bond market, as the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond dropped to 6.29 percent from 6.32 percent.
* True North Communications Inc agreed to buy Bozell, Kenyon & Eckhardt in a stock deal valued at about $440 million, creating the world's sixth-largest advertising company.
* Federal enforcement officials are sending a tough new message to hospital administrators about cheating on Federal health care cost reports.
* Companies searched for alternative ways to ship their packages as the United Parcel Service at the last minute sought to avert a walkout by the 185,000 members of its teamsters union.

* Apple Computer Inc advisor Steve Jobs, taking an active role in leading the search for the company's new chief executive, has unsuccessfully been trying to land Eastman Kodak Co chief executive George Fisher.
* The chief executives of many large corporations seek to block a proposed accounting rule that would require companies to show derivative securities on their balance sheets.

* Turner Broadcasting System's TBS superstation will essentially become a basic cable network at year's end, generating as much as $100 million in new revenue for its parent, Time Warner Inc, in the next few years.
* Sun Microsystems Inc is buying start-up company Diba, which creates technology for simple devices to surf the World Wide Web or send electronic mail.
* The House and Senate approved a tax cut offering a net reduction of $96 billion over the next five years.
* Senior monetary fund officials are angry that their warnings -- put in place after the Mexican peso's collapse -- went largely ignored for so long in Thailand's current monetary crisis.
* Shareholders of the Student Loan Marketing Association ousted the company's management by electing a dissident slate of directors.
* The U.S. economy slowed during the spring as consumers cut back on their spending, according to government data.
* U.S. railroads are increasingly looking to technology to help them win customers back from truckers.
